Issues.Title: `@tailwindcss/turbopack` reuses a compiler built from an older `source` when called again with the same mtime
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**
4.3.3 (`@tailwindcss/turbopack` 4.3.3). The same code is on `main` (d58099862).

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?**
Next.js 16.4.2 with Turbopack (also 16.4.1 and 16.5.0-canary.15), using `turbopack.rules: { "*.css": { loaders: ["@tailwindcss/turbopack"], as: "*.css" } }`.

**What version of Node.js are you using?**
24.21.0

**What browser are you using?**
N/A (build output)

**What operating system are you using?**
macOS 27 (arm64) locally; the production build ran on Vercel (Linux).

**Reproduction URL**
https://github.com/theravengroup/turbopack-stale-tailwind-css

`repro.sh` is the end-to-end repro with Next.js. `loader-direct.mjs` is the deterministic part: ~40 lines that call the loader directly, with no Next.js involved.

**Describe your issue**

The loader caches one compiler per `this.resource` in the worker process. It decides whether to rebuild that compiler by comparing the mtimes of the stylesheet and its full-rebuild dependencies, and it never compares the `source` argument. When the loader is called twice in the same process for the same file, with different `source` and an unchanged mtime, the second call reuses the compiler built from the first `source`. The output has the second call's scanned candidates, but the first call's `@theme`, `@layer` rules, `@font-face`, `@keyframes` and so on.

```js
// loader-direct.mjs (abridged): same file, same mtime, two different sources
await runLoader(`@import "tailwindcss"; :root { --repro-stylesheet: "v1" }`)
await runLoader(`@import "tailwindcss"; :root { --repro-stylesheet: "v2" }`)
// call 2 with v2 source -> output compiled from v1
```

This isn't hypothetical. Turbopack does exactly this after restoring its persistent build cache (`experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild`, on by default since Next.js 16.3; Vercel restores `.next/cache` between deployments):

1. When a commit changes both the stylesheet and a file the loader scans, Turbopack can run the loader with the cached `source` from the previous build before the stylesheet has been re-read.
2. It then runs the loader again with the content on disk. That second result is the one it keeps.
3. If both calls land in the same Node worker, the second one takes the "incremental" path and returns CSS built from the previous commit's stylesheet.

We shipped exactly that to production: the new components' utilities on top of the old theme, with missing `@font-face` and `@keyframes` rules. It reproduces locally about half the time with `TURBO_ENGINE_READ_CONCURRENCY=1` (see `repro.sh`).

`@tailwindcss/postcss` had the same gap and closed it in #20310 ("rebuilds when the input CSS changes but its mtime is unchanged"). The turbopack loader needs the same check:

```diff
 interface CacheEntry {
   mtimes: Map<string, number>
+  source: string | null
   compiler: null | Awaited<ReturnType<typeof compile>>
   scanner: null | Scanner
   candidates: Set<string>
   fullRebuildPaths: string[]
 }
@@ getContextFromCache
   let entry: CacheEntry = {
     mtimes: new Map<string, number>(),
+    source: null,
     compiler: null,
@@ after the mtime loop in tailwindLoader
+      // The mtimes above only track files on disk. The bundler can call the loader again for the
+      // same resource with a different `source` (Turbopack does after a persistent-cache
+      // restore), so also rebuild when the source itself changed.
+      if (context.source !== source) {
+        rebuildStrategy = 'full'
+        context.source = source
+      }
```

On the first call this marks the build `full`, but `isInitialBuild` already skips the rebuild, so nothing extra happens. With this change, `loader-direct.mjs` returns v2 for the second call, and the end-to-end repro went from 18/33 stale builds to 0/10.


Related: the Turbopack side (running the loader on the previous build's content after a cache restore) is filed as vercel/next.js#100326.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "`@tailwindcss/turbopack` reuses a compiler built from an older `source` when called again with the same mtime" (#20584)

Issues.Title: Avoid floating point noise when constant folding `calc()` and unit converstion
Issues.Body:
<!--

👋 Hey, thanks for your interest in contributing to Tailwind!

**Please ask first before starting work on any significant new features.**

It's never a fun experience to have your pull request declined after investing a lot of time and effort into a new feature. To avoid this from happening, we request that contributors create a discussion to first discuss any significant new features.

For more info, check out the contributing guide:

https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md

-->

## Summary

Constant folding on `constant-fold-declaration.ts` were computing every `calc()` fold and unit conversion, so decimal inputs leakead floating point noise into canonicalization

examples:

```js
// before
canonicalize('w-[calc(0.1rem+0.2rem)]') // 'w-[0.30000000000000004rem]'
canonicalize('w-[calc(0.3rem/0.1)]')    // 'w-[calc(0.3rem/0.1)]' (not folded)
canonicalize('w-[25.4mm]')              // 'w-[25.4mm]'
canonicalize('w-[12.7cm]')              // 'w-[12.7cm]'

// With `--spacing: 0.2rem`
canonicalize('w-[0.6rem]')              // 'w-[0.6rem]'
canonicalize('w-[1.4rem]')              // 'w-[1.4rem]'

// after
canonicalize('w-[calc(0.1rem+0.2rem)]') // 'w-[0.3rem]'
canonicalize('w-[calc(0.3rem/0.1)]')    // 'w-12'
canonicalize('w-[25.4mm]')              // 'w-24'
canonicalize('w-[12.7cm]')              // 'w-120'

// With `--spacing: 0.2rem`
canonicalize('w-[0.6rem]')              // 'w-3'
canonicalize('w-[1.4rem]')              // 'w-7'
```

the compiled css isn't affected, only canonicalization because it feeds the `canonicalize` CLI, the upgrade codemod and IntelliSense, so the noise could be written into users source files, it also made equivalent values compare as different: 

```js
// Before: the same length, three different canonical values
constantFoldDeclaration('1cm', 16)  // '37.79527559055118px'
constantFoldDeclaration('10mm', 16) // '37.795275590551185px'
constantFoldDeclaration('40q', 16)  // '37.795275590551185px'

// After
constantFoldDeclaration('1cm', 16)  // '37.7952755906px'
constantFoldDeclaration('10mm', 16) // '37.7952755906px'
constantFoldDeclaration('40q', 16)  // '37.7952755906px'
```

solution approach: 

the operands are already decimal string in the css, so this does just the math on those strings

- new decimals utility where a number is parsed from its written form into a int plus a scale, like `4.35 -> { int: 435, scale: 2 }`, and `and`, `sub`, `mul` and `div` work on int numbers, `div` returns a result only if it ends whitin 2 decimals, the same limit as the current implementation, any input that isn't a plain decimal, or any intermediate value that isn't a safe integer returns `null`
- unit conversion uses rational factors, `cm = ×4800/127`, `mm = ×480/127`, `q = ×120/127` and `pt = ×4/3`are exact multiplication plus one float division, round to 12 significant digits, so `1cm`, `10mm` and `40`q cannonicalize identically, `in`, `pc`, `rem`, `grad`, `turn`, `ms` and `khz` convert exactly, `rad` use `pi`, so it is computed with float and rounded to 12 significant digits, significant digits (not decimal places) keep the relative error the same at any magnitude, so a tiny converted value that a `calc()` multiplies back up stays correct, like `calc(0.00000000001pt * 1000000000000) → 10pt` instead of `0`, values that can't be written with 12 digits without an exponent aren't converted
- the spacing ration in `createSpacingCache` is exact with a fallback to the float ration for values that aren't 2 decimal multipliers, the fallback keeps line-height matching such as `28.5px / 4px = 7.125 → text-sm/[28.5px]` working
- unitless and unkown values are normalized as written intead of going through `Number`, so items behave like `1.50 → 1.5` and `-0 → 0`, this also stops output like `1e-7`, `1e+200px` and `Infinity`

stackblitz exmaple using `main` code: https://stackblitz.com/github/otarampinelli/tw-canon-repro?file=repro.mjs

## Test plan

• `src/utils/decimal.test.ts` every export, including each null case, unsafe integers, division by zero, maxDecimals, no exponent output, -0
• `src/constant-fold-declaration.test.ts` noise free `+ - * /` and nested re association, the 2 decimal division limit, rem at 14 and 18, exact conversions and `cm/mm/q` equivalence, no exponent notation, no overflow or precision loss, and rad rounding
• `src/canonicalize-candidates.test.ts` end-to-end rows from the table above, plus `rotate-[0.785398163397rad] → rotate-45 and rotate-[1rad]` staying arbitrary.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Avoid floating point noise when constant folding `calc()` and unit converstion" (#20585)

Issues.Title: @tailwindcss/turbopack serves stale CSS in `next dev` after editing the CSS file
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**

v4.3.3

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?**

Next.js 16.4.0 with Turbopack (`next dev`). The project was created with `create-next-app@16.4.0` (Tailwind enabled, default bundler), which sets up the `@tailwindcss/turbopack` loader in `next.config.ts`.

**What version of Node.js are you using?**

v25.2.1

**What browser are you using?**

Chrome

**What operating system are you using?**

macOS 26.4.1 

**Reproduction URL**

https://github.com/natefzz/tailwind-turbopack-stale-css

The README has the steps and a script (`check-stale.mjs`) that edits `globals.css` repeatedly and checks the CSS served by the dev server.

**Describe your issue**

With the `@tailwindcss/turbopack` loader added in #20367, editing the input CSS file during `next dev` makes the dev server keep serving the **previous** version of that CSS. Saving again without changing the content does not help; only restarting the dev server does. With `@tailwindcss/postcss` and the same Turbopack dev server, the problem goes away.

**What I think is happening**

The loader caches one compiler per CSS file and decides whether to rebuild it by comparing **mtimes on disk**, not the **source it receives**. I added logging to `dist/index.js` (input value, `statSync(resourcePath).mtimeMs`, rebuild decision, output). For a single save from `#ffffff` to `#ff0000`, Turbopack invoked the loader twice:

```
CALL  input=#ffffff  fileMtime=1791964831511.853   <- old source, but the mtime is already new
      decide=full    newCompiler=true              <- compiler rebuilt from the OLD source
      OUTPUT=#ffffff
CALL  input=#ff0000  fileMtime=1791964831511.853   <- correct source
      decide=incremental newCompiler=false         <- mtime unchanged, stale compiler reused
      OUTPUT=#ffffff                               <- stale output
```

The first call gets the previous source but already sees the new mtime, so it rebuilds the compiler from the old source and records the new mtime. The second call gets the correct source, but the mtime matches, so it reuses that stale compiler.

I'm not sure why Turbopack first runs the loader with the previous source. My guess is that the loader registers both file dependencies and a context dependency on the project directory, which gives two invalidation paths. As far as I can tell, the mtime check works with webpack, which calls the loader once with fresh content, but it doesn't hold up under Turbopack's behavior.

**Possible fix**

Store the last source (or a hash of it) on the cache entry, and force a full rebuild whenever `source` differs, in addition to the existing mtime checks. I'm happy to open a PR if this direction sounds right.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "@tailwindcss/turbopack serves stale CSS in `next dev` after editing the CSS file" (#20581)

Issues.Title: Rebuild `@tailwindcss/turbopack` and `@tailwindcss/webpack` when the input CSS changes
Issues.Body:
This PR fixes an issue where `next dev` with the `@tailwindcss/turbopack` loader keeps serving the CSS of the previous edit after you edit the CSS file. Only a restart of the dev server shows the latest version.

Fixes https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/issues/20581

The loader caches a compiler for each CSS file. It only does a full rebuild when the mtime of the input file (or of one of its dependencies) changes. After a save, Turbopack can run the loader two times:

1. With the previous version of the CSS file. The file on disk already has the new mtime, so we did a full rebuild from the old source, and stored the new mtime.
2. With the new version of the CSS file. The mtime did not change since the first call, so we did an incremental build with the stale compiler of the first call.

The loader registers the folders that it scans as context dependencies, and the CSS file is in one of them (e.g. `app/`). So one save invalidates the loader in two ways, and the first run can still get the previous content of the file.

`@tailwindcss/postcss` had the same problem with Turbopack (https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/17554), and it compares the input CSS with the input CSS of the last build since https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20310. The loader now does the same: it stores the source on the cache entry, and does a full rebuild when the source changes.

`@tailwindcss/turbopack` is a copy of `@tailwindcss/webpack`, so the webpack loader gets the same fix. With webpack, the problem shows up when a loader that runs before ours changes the CSS, but not the input file. For example, `sass-loader` inlines a partial, and you edit that partial.

The matrix of the integration tests in CI had no `turbopack` entry, so the tests in `integrations/turbopack` never ran in CI. This PR adds it.

## Test plan

- Added an integration test to `integrations/turbopack/loader.test.ts`. It edits `app/globals.css` three times during `next dev`, and checks that the served CSS has each edit. On `main` (with Next.js 16.4.1), the served CSS still has `.custom-1` after the first edit. With this change, it passes.
- Added an integration test to `integrations/webpack/loader.test.ts`, with a loader before `@tailwindcss/webpack` that inlines `src/partial.css`. In watch mode, it edits that partial. On `main`, the output keeps `.partial-1`. With this change, it passes.
- Called the built loaders directly, like Turbopack does: first with the previous source after the file changed on disk, then with the new source. On `main`, the second call returns the CSS of the previous version. With this change, each call returns the CSS of the source that it gets.
- `pnpm run build` passes, and all tests in `integrations/turbopack/loader.test.ts` and `integrations/webpack/loader.test.ts` pass.

Issues.Title: Ensure `@tailwindcss/turbopack` rebuilds when the input CSS changes but its mtime is unchanged
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #20581

The `@tailwindcss/turbopack` loader decides between an incremental and a full rebuild by comparing mtimes only. Turbopack can run the loader with the previous source after the input file's mtime has already changed, and then again with the current source. The first call rebuilds the compiler from the stale source and records the new mtime, so the second call sees an unchanged mtime and reuses that stale compiler. As a result, `next dev` keeps serving the CSS from one revision before the latest edit.

This is the same "one revision behind" symptom that was fixed for `@tailwindcss/postcss` in #17554, and `@tailwindcss/postcss` has also compared the input CSS with the previous compile since #20310. This PR adds the same inputCss check to the Turbopack loader, which was ported from the webpack loader and lacks this check.

## Test plan

Added an integration test that edits the input CSS file during `next dev` and checks that the served CSS reflects each edit.

Without the fix, the new test fails because the served CSS still contains the previous edit:

```
AssertionError: expected '/* [project]/app/globals.css.css [app…' to contain 'token-two'
```

With the fix, both Turbopack tests pass:

```sh
pnpm build
pnpm test:integrations turbopack
```

Issues.Title: Round constant folded nums to get rid of floating point noise
Issues.Body:
<!--

👋 Hey, thanks for your interest in contributing to Tailwind!

**Please ask first before starting work on any significant new features.**

It's never a fun experience to have your pull request declined after investing a lot of time and effort into a new feature. To avoid this from happening, we request that contributors create a discussion to first discuss any significant new features.

For more info, check out the contributing guide:

https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md

-->

## Summary


This solution is addressing the floating point noise on calc that makes items like `w-[calc(0.1px+0.2px)]` turn into a value with a floating point noise like `w-[0.30000000000000004px]`, it address `+`, `-`, `*` and `/` calculations

This is fixed with a `roundFloatNoise` helper that rounds the computed number to 15 significant digits and converts it back with `Number()` which drops the noise and any trailing zeros, integers are return as it is, rounding uses significant digits intead of decimal places, so small values aren't erased, for example, `calc(0.000001 * 0.000001)` keeps its value `(1e-12)` and doesn't collapse to `0`

division is rounded before the existing two-decimal precision check. Before, `calc(0.3px / 3)` computed `0.09999999999999999`, failed that check, and stayed unfolded, now it folds to `0.1px`

```js
before:
w-[calc(0.1px+0.2px)]            -> w-[0.30000000000000004px]
w-[calc(0.3px-0.1px)]            -> w-[0.19999999999999998px]
w-[calc(0.1rem*3)]               -> w-[0.30000000000000004rem]
w-[calc(1.1*1.1)]                -> w-[1.2100000000000002]
opacity-[calc(0.7+0.1)]          -> opacity-[0.7999999999999999]
w-[calc(0.1px+calc(0.2px+var(--foo)))] -> w-[calc(0.30000000000000004px+var(--foo))]
w-[calc(0.3px/3)]                -> w-[calc(0.3px/3)]   (left unfolded)

now:
w-[calc(0.1px+0.2px)]            -> w-[0.3px]
w-[calc(0.3px-0.1px)]            -> w-[0.2px]
w-[calc(0.1rem*3)]               -> w-[0.3rem]
w-[calc(1.1*1.1)]                -> w-[1.21]
opacity-[calc(0.7+0.1)]          -> opacity-[0.8]
w-[calc(0.1px+calc(0.2px+var(--foo)))] -> w-[calc(0.3px+var(--foo))]
w-[calc(0.3px/3)]                -> w-[0.1px]
```

Reproduction: https://stackblitz.com/github/otarampinelli/tw-canon-repro?file=README.md

related to  #20221 and #20563 which fixed similar problems

## Test plan

- added cases for each operation (`+`, `-`, `*`, `/`) to `constant-fold-declaration.test.ts`, covering unitless values, values with units, and nested `calc(…)` with `var(--foo)`, the new noise affected cases fail on `main` and pass with this change
- added canonicalization cases for `+`, `-`, `*` and `/` to `canonicalize-candidates.test.ts`
- division now rounds before the two decimal precision check, so `calc(0.3px / 3)` (`0.09999999999999999` on `main`) folds to `0.1px` instead of staying unfolded
- added a division after a rounded fold: `calc(calc(0.1px + 0.2px) / 2)` → `0.15px`
- added regression cases so small values aren't rounded to `0` (e.g. `calc(calc(0.00000000001 * 1) * 100000000000)`), so the result stays unfolded with its value intact (`calc(1e-11 * 100000000000)`), because exponent notation isn't parsed by the folder

`pnpm vitest run packages/tailwindcss/src/constant-fold-declaration.test.ts`
`pnpm vitest run packages/tailwindcss/src/canonicalize-candidates.test.ts`
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Round constant folded nums to get rid of floating point noise" (#20580)

Issues.Title: Bump Bun to 1.4 so macOS standalone binaries get a valid code signature
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #20544.

`bun build --compile` in Bun 1.3.14 writes the ad-hoc Mach-O signature with the hash of the last 4 KiB page taken over a zero-padded page, not the real bytes. `codesign --verify` reports an invalid signature, and macOS 27 checks that page at launch and kills `tailwindcss-macos-arm64`. Bun 1.4.1 and later sign the real bytes.

This bumps `bun` and `@types/bun` in `@tailwindcss/standalone` from `^1.3.14` to `^1.4.1`. The lockfile now resolves Bun 1.4.3. The fix reaches users with the next release, because the binaries are built at release time.

## Test plan

I built the standalone binaries before and after the bump on Linux (`cd packages/@tailwindcss-standalone && pnpm build`) and hashed every 4096-byte page of `dist/tailwindcss-macos-arm64` against its `LC_CODE_SIGNATURE` CodeDirectory:

| | Bun | bad pages | last page hash matches the zero-padded page |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 1.3.14 | `[(17905, 2736)]` | yes |
| this PR | 1.4.3 | none | no |

I could not run the binary on macOS 27, so the launch kill itself is not tested here.

Also checked with the bump: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes, the build finishes for all 7 targets, and the `tailwindcss-linux-x64` binary builds `@import "tailwindcss"` and generates `.flex`, `.p-4` and `hover:underline` for a small HTML file.

`dist/tailwindcss-macos-arm64` grows from 73.9 MB to 81.3 MB.

I did not run `integrations/cli/standalone.test.ts`, because it needs `pnpm pack` tarballs of every package, including the WASM build.

I am new to open source, and this pull request was made with AI assistance.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Bump Bun to 1.4 so macOS standalone binaries get a valid code signature" (#20578)

Issues.Title: Fix out of memory error in the canonicalize tests on macOS CI
Issues.Body:
This PR fixes the `macOS` job of CI on `main`, which fails with `JavaScript heap out of memory` in `packages/tailwindcss/src/canonicalize-candidates.test.ts`. It failed in both attempts of the run for https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/commit/92172d387827f1160ebe7415d80c542933c0e9d7, and earlier for https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20540.

The test file cached every design system that it built in a module-level map for the whole run. Each design system uses ~30MB of memory, so the heap grows with each test that has its own CSS input. After a forced GC, the heap at the end of the file was:

| Commit | Design systems | Heap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20417 | 57 | 1886 MB |
| https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20563 | 61 | 1982 MB |
| `main` | 64 | 2137 MB |

The macOS runners have a default heap limit of ~2GB, so the file now crosses it. The memory of one design system did not change in recent commits, only the number of design systems.

Now, the file keeps only the 32 most recently used design systems. The strategies of the file (`default`, `with-variant`, `important`) cycle through the same ~30 inputs, so a smaller cache evicts each design system right before it is used again. That makes the file ~70% slower (124 builds instead of 64). With 32, the file builds 66 design systems.

## Test plan

- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=2048 vitest run src/canonicalize-candidates.test.ts` runs out of memory on `main`, and passes with this change. It also passes with a limit of 1280 MB.
- The duration of the file stays the same (~13s locally).
- `vitest run --project tailwindcss` passes.

Issues.Title: `canonicalizeCandidates` with `collapse: true`: time doubles with each linked class
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "`canonicalizeCandidates` with `collapse: true`: time doubles with each linked class" (#20557)

Issues.Title: Canonicalization: avoid exponential collapse when a utility sets many properties
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #20557.

`canonicalizeCandidates(…, { collapse: true })` took time that doubled with every class in a group of linked candidates.

`collapseGroup` links two candidates when their `otherUtilities` sets (possible replacements) share an entry, and then tries every combination (2^n − n − 1) of each linked group, computing a signature for each. A static utility that sets many properties ends up in the `otherUtilities` of every candidate that sets one of those properties. For example `sr-only` and `not-sr-only` link `relative`, `mt-1`, `w-64`, `overflow-x-auto`, `whitespace-nowrap`, … and a project `@utility` used as a component class does the same, even when the class list doesn't use it.

But such a replacement can never be picked. Its signature can only equal the signature of a combination if every property it sets is also set by a candidate in that combination, and each of those candidates has the replacement in its own `otherUtilities`. `sr-only` also sets `clip-path` and `border-width`, which none of those candidates set, so no combination can ever match it.

This PR changes two things:

1. Before linking, drop every replacement whose properties aren't covered by the candidates that list it. This only uses the property lookups that are already computed, and it only removes replacements that can't match, so the replacements that do get used stay the same. With the impossible ones gone, the giant linked groups split up into the small groups you'd expect (e.g. `overflow-x-*` + `overflow-y-*` → `overflow-*`), so the number of combinations stays small.
2. In the combination loop, skip the (expensive) signature computation for a combination when the intersection of its possible replacements is empty.

Results with the reproduction from the issue (Node 20, same design system per row; times are for one `canonicalizeCandidates` call):

| Case | Classes | Before | After |
| --- | --: | --: | --: |
| A: default theme | 10 | 102 ms | 19 ms |
| | 12 | 369 ms | 22 ms |
| | 14 | 1,374 ms | 20 ms |
| B: default theme + `pill` `@utility` | 12 | 348 ms | 19 ms |
| | 14 | 1,709 ms | 24 ms |
| | 15 | 3,487 ms | 29 ms |
| | 16 | 7,278 ms | 26 ms |

The output was the same before and after for every row, including `text-sm leading-5` → `text-sm/5`, which the issue mentions breaking when the lookup was restricted to matching values instead.

One limit: if a class list really does cover every property of a big utility, its candidates are still linked through it, and that group is still enumerated as before. That's the existing behaviour, and it's much rarer than the cases above.

## Test plan

- Added a regression test with 23 classes linked through `sr-only`, `not-sr-only` and a `pill` `@utility`. It checks the collapsed output (`text-sm leading-5` → `text-sm/5`, everything else untouched) and that it finishes in under 5 s. It takes ~0.8 s on this branch. Without the fix I stopped it after more than 3 minutes.
- `pnpm vitest run packages/tailwindcss/src`: 43 files, 5017 tests passing (this includes all 1805 existing canonicalization tests, whose outputs are unchanged).
- `prettier --check` on the changed files; `tsc` reports no errors for the changed files.

Issues.Title: Reject arbitrary values with unbalanced parens or brackets
Issues.Body: ## Summary Candidates with an unclosed `(` or `[` inside an arbitray value are accepted and generated invalid css: ```css `w-[calc(20px]` -> `width: calc()20px;` `w-[(]` -> `width: ();` ``` Tailwind play with the bug reproduced: https://play.tailwindcss.com/vQyd5Lh4bz Why this was happening: 1. `isValidArbitrary` documents that unbalanced values are not allowed, but it never checked that every `(` and `[` was closed, and it ignored a mismatched closer such as `(]`. 2. the parser validated the value after `decodeArbitraryValue`, and the value parser turns `calc(20px` into `calc()20px`, so the validator only saw a balanced string. This pr: - Makes `isValidArbitrary` return `false` for a mismatched closing char and for any unclosed `(` or `[` at the end of the value, a mismatched `}` is still tolerated, since `{` is not tracked on the stack, e.g. `var(--a, {})` - validates the raw value before decoding, via a small `decodeValidArbitraryValue` helper at all places where an arbitrary value is parsed, like arbitrary properties, utility values, modifiers , arbitrary variants and functional variants suck `[...]` and `(...)` this change is also making the js parser agree with the rust scanner, which already rejects unbalanced brackets (check `arbitrary_value_machine.rs`), this bug is reachable wherever the js parser receives strings directly, such tailwind play or `compile().build([...])` ## Test plan - added test to `candidate.test.ts` covering unbalanced values for utility values, arbitrary properties, modifiers, arbitrary variants and functional variants, they fail on `main` and pass with the change made here - Some existent tests contained unbalanced inputs taht only passed because the value parser repaired or dropped the bad paren `pnpm vitest run src/candidate.test.ts` `pnpm vitest run src/index.test.ts`

Issues.Title: Drop nested rules that put a combinator after a pseudo-element
Issues.Body:
Fixes #20571

## Summary

A functional utility with a nested child rule, like `@utility bg-* { & > * { … } }`, used under a pseudo-element variant (`selection:`, `marker:`, `backdrop:`) gets flattened in `handleNesting` into `.selection\:bg-red-500::selection > *`. A pseudo-element can only be followed by pseudo-classes, so that rule never matches, and Lightning CSS prints the "Pseudo-elements like '::before' or '::after' can't be followed by selectors like 'Delim('>')'" warning on every build.

When a nested rule is flattened, each selector that ends up with a combinator right after a pseudo-element (`::x`, functional ones like `::part(x)`, and the legacy `:before`/`:after`/`:first-line`/`:first-letter`) is dropped. If none of the selectors are left, the rule is dropped. Pseudo-classes after a pseudo-element (`.a::part(x):hover`) and combinators before one (`.a ::selection`) are untouched, and user-authored top-level selectors are never rewritten.

One case is not covered here: for `before:`/`after:` the parent rule has declarations, so the child stays nested as `& > *` and Lightning CSS already drops it without a warning.

## Test plan

- New `combinators after a pseudo-element` cases in `ast.test.ts`, and a `selection:`/`marker:`/`hover:` case for the issue's utility in `utilities.test.ts`. 4 of them fail without the change; the two "keeps" cases pass on both and guard against over-matching.
- `npx vitest run` in `packages/tailwindcss`: 5108 passed, 1 skipped.
- `prettier --check` on the changed files.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Drop nested rules that put a combinator after a pseudo-element" (#20573)

Issues.Title: A utility's nested rule under a pseudo-element variant is written as ::selection > * and dropped with a warning
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?** 
v4.3.3 (`tailwindcss`, `@tailwindcss/vite` 4.3.3, Vite 8.3.2)

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?** 
Vite 8.3.2 with `@tailwindcss/vite`

**What version of Node.js are you using?**
 v22.14.0

**What browser are you using?** 
n/a (build output)

**What operating system are you using?** 
Linux (WSL2)

**Reproduction URL:** 
https://play.tailwindcss.com/fj2ehk4puO

**Describe your issue**

A custom utility with a nested child rule:

```css
@utility bg-* {
  & > * {
    --nearest-bg: --value(--color-*);
  }
}
```

used under a pseudo-element variant, such as `selection:bg-red-500` (also `backdrop:`, `before:`, `after:`, `marker:`), makes the build print:

```
Found 1 warning while optimizing generated CSS:

Issue #1:
  .selection\:bg-red-500 ::selection > * {
                                     ^-- Pseudo-elements like '::before' or '::after' can't be followed by selectors like 'Delim('>')'
```

The variant is applied to every nested rule of the matched utility. The nesting is then flattened by pasting the parent selector in for `&`, which gives `.x::selection > *`. Under CSS Nesting, `&` cannot represent a pseudo-element, so that rule matches nothing and could be dropped quietly. Today lightningcss drops it with the warning above. For `before:`/`after:` the rule is dropped silently and an empty `.after\:bg-white:after{content:var(--tw-content)}` remains. For `marker:` the output keeps `::-webkit-details-marker>*` with no warning.

A utility cannot opt out on its side: it never sees which variants the class carries, and `@variant` inside it cannot name a negated pseudo-element variant.

**Expected:** a nested rule whose parent selector ends in a pseudo-element is dropped while flattening, with no warning, as Tailwind already does silently for its own `selection:space-x-4` (which ships a dead `:where()` rule).
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "A utility's nested rule under a pseudo-element variant is written as ::selection > * and dropped with a warning" (#20571)

Issues.Title: Drop nested rules that put a combinator after a pseudo-element
Issues.Body:
This PR fixes an issue where a utility with a nested rule, used with a pseudo-element variant, results in a selector that can never match anything.

```css
@utility bg-* {
  & > * {
    --nearest-bg: --value(--color-*);
  }
}
```

With `selection:bg-red-500`, the nested rule was flattened to:

```css
.selection\:bg-red-500::selection > * {
  --nearest-bg: var(--color-red-500);
}
```

A pseudo-element can only be followed by pseudo-classes, so this never matches. Lightning CSS drops these rules, but warns about each of them on every build:

```
Pseudo-elements like '::before' or '::after' can't be followed by selectors like 'Delim('>')'
```

The same happens for `backdrop:` and `marker:`. For `marker:` the `::-webkit-details-marker > *` rule was even kept in the output.

When we flatten nested rules in `handleNesting`, we now drop each selector that puts a combinator after a pseudo-element (e.g. `::selection`, `::part(…)`, vendor-prefixed ones like `::-webkit-details-marker`, and the legacy `:before`, `:after`, `:first-line` and `:first-letter`). This also covers `:is(…)` and `:where(…)` when all of their arguments are dead, which means that built-in utilities like `selection:space-x-4` no longer emit an empty `:where()` rule after optimization.

If none of the selectors are left, then the declarations of the rule are dropped. Rules nested inside of it are still processed, because they can still match (e.g. `:is(&, .fallback)`). This also applies to rules inside hoistable at-rules such as `@media` and `@scope`. An `@scope` is only dropped when its `<scope-start>` selector can never match. Empty `@layer` rules are kept (without the dead selector), because they can establish the layer order.

Things that are intentionally left alone:

- Pseudo-classes after a pseudo-element (e.g. `.a::before:hover`).
- Combinators before a pseudo-element (e.g. `.a > ::before`).
- Top-level selectors written by the user (e.g. `.a::selection > * { … }`).
- Unknown pseudo-elements, such as framework specific deep combinators like `::ng-deep` (Angular) and `::v-deep` (Vue 2). Another compiler rewrites them later on.
- `before:` and `after:`. The parent rule has declarations (`content: var(--tw-content)`), so the nested rule stays nested as `& > *`. Browsers and Lightning CSS already drop it without a warning.

I also moved the `isPseudoElement` helper from `canonicalize-candidates.ts` to `selector-parser.ts` so both places can use it.

Fixes: https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/issues/20571
Closes #20573

## Test plan

1. Added tests to `ast.test.ts` for dropped selectors, partially dropped selector lists, selectors that must be kept, unknown pseudo-elements, and nested rules, `@scope` and `@layer` rules inside a dropped rule.
2. Added a test to `utilities.test.ts` for the issue's utility with `selection:`, `backdrop:` and `hover:`.
3. Existing tests still pass.
4. Built the issue's example and ran it through Lightning CSS: no warnings anymore.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Drop nested rules that put a combinator after a pseudo-element" (#20575)

Issues.Title: @tailwindcss/postcss in a Vite production build: relative url() from imported CSS is not rewritten (optimize drops source.input.file)
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**

v4.3.3 (`tailwindcss` and `@tailwindcss/postcss`). Also reproduces with `0.0.0-insiders.1a38f84`.

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?**

Vite 8.3.4, with `@tailwindcss/postcss` through `postcss.config.mjs`

**What version of Node.js are you using?**

v22.23.3

**What browser are you using?**

N/A (build output)

**What operating system are you using?**

Linux

**Reproduction URL**

https://github.com/Chaosnico9000/tailwind-postcss-import-url-repro

**Describe your issue**

A package ships a font stylesheet with relative URLs, and the app imports it from its Tailwind entry CSS:

```css
/* example-font/fonts.css */
@font-face {
  font-family: "Example Sans";
  src: url("./fonts/ExampleSans.woff2") format("woff2");
}
```

```css
/* src/index.css */
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "example-font/fonts.css";
```

```js
// postcss.config.mjs
export default { plugins: { "@tailwindcss/postcss": {} } };
```

`vite` (dev) serves the font correctly. `vite build` does not emit it: the CSS keeps `url(./fonts/ExampleSans.woff2)`, which 404s at runtime, and the only trace is a warning:

```text
./fonts/ExampleSans.woff2 referenced in ./fonts/ExampleSans.woff2 didn't resolve at build time, it will remain unchanged to be resolved at runtime
```

Expected: the font is emitted to `dist/assets` and the URL rewritten. That is what happens with `@tailwindcss/vite`, in dev, with `NODE_ENV=development vite build`, and with `optimize: false` (all four are in the repro). `transformAssetUrls: false` makes no difference. It is not specific to packages either: `@import "./fonts/local.css"` with a `url("./font.woff2")` next to it fails the same way.

This is the symptom of #16636 / #16700. #16636 was closed by #16965 (URL rewriting for stylesheets that Tailwind inlines itself, tested with `postcss-cli`), #16700 after #18321 added `transformAssetUrls`. Neither covers Vite: the original repro from #16636, updated to 4.3.3 and Vite 8.3.4, still prints all eight warnings on `vite build` and emits the fonts with `NODE_ENV=development`.

**Why it happens**

1. Vite prepends its own `postcss-import` to the PostCSS plugin list, so the `@import`s are already inlined when `@tailwindcss/postcss` runs. Tailwind's own `@import` handling (and with it `transformAssetUrls`) never sees them. Vite also appends its URL-rewrite plugin, which resolves each `url()` against the declaration's `source.input.file`. Before Tailwind runs, that is still the imported file (`example-font/fonts.css`).
2. Without optimization, `@tailwindcss/postcss` rebuilds the PostCSS tree with [`cssAstToPostCssAst(postcss, tailwindCssAst, root.source)`](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/blob/1a38f848f0afb04c6a7b2627d786afc8d8fcd974/packages/@tailwindcss-postcss/src/index.ts#L322-L327), which keeps each node's original source. That is why dev works.
3. [`optimize` defaults to `NODE_ENV === 'production'`](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/blob/1a38f848f0afb04c6a7b2627d786afc8d8fcd974/packages/@tailwindcss-postcss/src/index.ts#L75), which `vite build` sets. The [optimized path](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/blob/1a38f848f0afb04c6a7b2627d786afc8d8fcd974/packages/@tailwindcss-postcss/src/index.ts#L304-L321) serializes the AST, runs Lightning CSS, and reparses the result with `postcss.parse(optimized.code, result.opts)`. Every node now has `src/index.css` as its input file.
4. Vite looks for `./fonts/ExampleSans.woff2` next to `src/index.css`, finds nothing, and leaves the URL unchanged.

A PostCSS plugin that logs `decl.source.input.file` for the `src` declaration, placed before and after Tailwind, shows it:

```text
# NODE_ENV=production (default for vite build)
before ./example-font/fonts.css url("./fonts/ExampleSans.woff2") format("woff2")
after ./src/index.css url(./fonts/ExampleSans.woff2)format("woff2")

# NODE_ENV=development
before ./example-font/fonts.css url("./fonts/ExampleSans.woff2") format("woff2")
after ./example-font/fonts.css url("./fonts/ExampleSans.woff2") format("woff2")
```

**Workaround**

`"@tailwindcss/postcss": { optimize: false }` (Vite minifies the CSS anyway), or importing the font CSS from JavaScript instead of from the Tailwind entry. Switching to `@tailwindcss/vite` also works, but is not always an option (see #16636, where Sass was the reason).

**Possible fixes**

- In the optimize path, rebase relative `url()` in declarations whose source file differs from the root's input file before handing the CSS to Lightning CSS, as is already done for stylesheets Tailwind inlines itself.
- Or carry the source mapping through Lightning CSS (`optimize()` already accepts an input map) and restore `source` on the reparsed nodes.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "@tailwindcss/postcss in a Vite production build: relative url() from imported CSS is not rewritten (optimize drops source.input.file)" (#20570)

Issues.Title: Rewrite `url(…)`s of stylesheets inlined before `@tailwindcss/postcss` in optimized builds
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/issues/20570

Vite adds its own `postcss-import` before the PostCSS plugins of the user. Thus, when `@tailwindcss/postcss` runs, the `@import`-ed stylesheets are already inlined. Their relative `url(…)`s are still relative to their own file. At the end, Vite resolves each `url(…)` against the `source.input.file` of its declaration.

Without optimization, we keep the `source` of each node (since https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/17775), so this works. With optimization, we parse the output of Lightning CSS again, and every node gets the input file as its `source`. `optimize` is on by default when `NODE_ENV` is `production`, and `vite build` sets it. Vite then looks for the asset next to the input file, does not find it, and keeps the URL as it is:

```
./fonts/ExampleSans.woff2 referenced in ./fonts/ExampleSans.woff2 didn't resolve at build time, it will remain unchanged to be resolved at runtime
```

This is the problem that https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/issues/16636 and https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/issues/16700 reported. https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/16965 fixed URL rewriting only for the stylesheets that we inline ourselves. `transformAssetUrls` (https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/18321) has no effect here.

## Solution

When we optimize, we now rewrite the relative `url(…)`s of declarations that come from another file, so that they are relative to the input file. This is the same rewrite that we do for the stylesheets that we inline ourselves. After the rewrite, the URLs match the `source` that the optimized nodes get.

- We rewrite the AST that we get from PostCSS, before we compile it. The stylesheets that we load ourselves are not in that AST yet, so we do not rewrite their URLs two times.
- Without optimization, nothing changes, because the nodes keep their `source`.
- `transformAssetUrls: false` disables the rewrite.

To share the code, `rewriteUrls` in `@tailwindcss/node` now uses a new `rewriteUrlsInAst` function. A callback gives it the base folder of each declaration.

This also changes optimized builds of other setups that run `postcss-import` before `@tailwindcss/postcss`, like `postcss-cli`. Their URLs are now relative to the input file, like the URLs of the stylesheets that we inline ourselves.

## Test plan

- Added unit tests in `packages/@tailwindcss-postcss/src/index.test.ts`. They run `postcss-import` before the plugin with `optimize` on, with `optimize` off, and with `transformAssetUrls: false`. The test with `optimize` on fails on `main`.
- Added an integration test in `integrations/postcss/url-rewriting.test.ts`. It runs `vite build` with `@tailwindcss/postcss` in a PostCSS config. Without this change, Vite emits no fonts and the test fails. With this change, it passes.
- `pnpm vitest run`: 5598 passed.
- `pnpm vitest --root=./integrations run` on `postcss/url-rewriting`, `vite/url-rewriting`, `postcss/index`, `postcss/source`, `postcss/plugins`, `postcss/config`, `postcss/core-as-postcss-plugin` and `postcss/multi-root`: all passed. I did not run `postcss/next.test.ts`.
- Built a Vite 8.2.0 project with a font CSS file in a package and one in a local folder. With `optimize: true`, the fonts are now emitted to `dist/assets` and the URLs are rewritten, the same as with `optimize: false`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Rewrite `url(…)`s of stylesheets inlined before `@tailwindcss/postcss` in optimized builds" (#20576)

Issues.Title: Don't collapse utilities into a utility with other theme variables
Issues.Body:
This PR fixes an issue where `canonicalizeCandidates(…, { collapse: true })` replaces a group of utilities with a utility that uses a different theme variable. The two variables only have the same value by default.

Given this theme:

```css
@theme {
  --spacing-card: 1rem;
  --spacing-other: 1rem;
}
```

| Input              | Before    | After                         |
| ------------------ | --------- | ----------------------------- |
| `mt-card mb-card`  | `my-4`    | `my-card`                     |
| `w-card h-card`    | `size-4`  | `size-card`                   |
| `mt-card mb-other` | `my-4`    | `mt-card mb-other`            |
| `w-card h-other`   | `size-4`  | `w-card h-other`              |
| `mt-card mb-4`     | `my-4`    | `mt-card mb-4`                |
| `p-card px-other`  | `p-card`  | `p-card px-other`             |

The results on the left render differently once one of the variables changes, e.g. in `.dark`, in a media query, or in a class.

## The cause

Signatures inline theme variables to their default value. This is correct for single candidates (e.g. `text-[var(--color-red-500)]` → `text-red-500`). But `var(--spacing-card)` and `calc(var(--spacing) * 4)` then both become `1rem`, so the collapse step can't see which variable a utility uses.

## The fix

A new cache compiles a utility the same way as its signature, and records the theme variables that are inlined in each declaration. The collapse step only uses this after the signature of a replacement already matches. Then each declaration of the replacement must use the same theme variables as the candidates it replaces.

A declaration without theme variables can still become one with theme variables. This is the same as for single candidates (`mt-[16px]` → `mt-4`), and it keeps existing results like:

- `[width:16px] [height:16px]` → `size-4`
- `[font-size:14px] [line-height:1.625]` → `text-sm/relaxed`
- `mt-[1px] mb-[1px]` → `my-px`
- `text-sm leading-5` → `text-sm/5`

No existing test expectation changes.

## Performance

The theme variables are only computed for a replacement whose signature already matches, and they are cached. With 10 class lists and the full default theme, the extra compiles take about 0.35ms of about 28ms on the first call (about 1%). Repeated calls do no extra work.

## Test plan

- Added a regression test for the cases in the table above
- All existing tests in `packages/tailwindcss` pass
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Don't collapse utilities into a utility with other theme variables" (#20574)

Issues.Title: Don't let quotes in Pug regex literals hide the end of an attribute list
Issues.Body:
This is a follow-up to https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20547.

That PR tracks strings inside Pug attribute lists, so that brackets in values like `a(title="a (b")` are ignored. But a quote that isn't a string delimiter, like the `"` in a regex such as `input(pattern=/"/.source)`, opened a string that never closed. That string hid the `)` of the attribute list. The list stayed open, so dots in class shorthands on later lines were not turned into spaces, and classes like `underline` in `span.underline.font-bold` were not extracted.

```pug
input(pattern=/"/.source)
span.underline.font-bold km
```

## Solution

Only template literals can span lines in JavaScript. So when a `'` or `"` string reaches the end of its line without a closing quote, it was not a string. In that case, we go back to just after the quote and scan the rest of the line again, with quotes as plain text. Each line is scanned at most twice, so this stays linear.

Detecting regex literals directly needs a JavaScript tokenizer, because a `/` can also be a division. This approach also covers other unpaired quotes, like `// don't cache` in a `script.` block.

The regression is not released yet, so there is no changelog entry: the existing entry of https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/pull/20547 covers it.

## Test plan

Added cases to `test_unbalanced_brackets_in_quoted_attribute_values` in `pug.rs`. They fail without this change.

```
cargo test -p tailwindcss-oxide
```
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Don't let quotes in Pug regex literals hide the end of an attribute list" (#20572)

Issues.Title: Underline the correct occurrence of an unsupported type in `--value(…)`
Issues.Body: ## Summary When an unsupported bare value data type is repeated in `--value(…)`, every warning underlines the first occurrence: ```css @utility paint-* { paint: --value(color, [color], color); } ``` Before, both warnings pointed at the first `color`: ``` --value(color,[color],color) ^^^^^ ``` This happened because the offset was found by replacing every word matching the type with a sentinel in a cloned node and then calling `indexOf` on the printed result, which always returns the first match. Now the offset is computed from the node's position instead: thame, plus the `(`, plus the printed length of the arguments before it. Each warning points at its own occurrence: ``` --value(color,[color],color) ^^^^^ --value(color,[color],color) ^^^^^ ``` ## Test plan Added a test in `packages/tailwindcss/src/utilities.test.ts`. It spies on `console.warn` and checks that the two warnings underline the first and the last color respectively. ``` cd packages/tailwindcss pnpm vitest run src/utilities.test.ts -t "repeated unsupported data type" ``` ## Evidences https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-yq34h5eo?file=input.css before fix: after fix:
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Underline the correct occurrence of an unsupported type in `--value(…)`" (#20554)

Issues.Title: `canonicalize`: `console.log` of a plugin lands in stdout, before the results
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**

v4.3.3, with `@tailwindcss/cli` and with the standalone CLI. On `main` (de2255b), `packages/@tailwindcss-cli/src/commands/canonicalize/index.ts` still loads the design system in the process that writes the results to `process.stdout`.

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?**

None. `tailwindcss canonicalize` of `@tailwindcss/cli` 4.3.3.

**What version of Node.js are you using?**

v26.10.0

**What browser are you using?**

N/A

**What operating system are you using?**

Linux

**Reproduction URL**

https://gist.github.com/rubas/92e64c757e6e51d98cc7cd7e9f60ec75

**Describe your issue**

`tailwindcss canonicalize` writes its results to stdout. When a plugin of the CSS entry calls `console.log` while it loads, that text lands in the same stream, before the results. A tool that reads the results gets one line too many, and the JSON output is no longer valid JSON.

`plugin.mjs`:

```js
export default function () {
  console.log("hello from a plugin")
}
```

`app.css`:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@plugin "./plugin.mjs";
```

```
$ npx tailwindcss canonicalize --css app.css "p-4 px-2 py-2"
hello from a plugin
p-2

$ npx tailwindcss canonicalize --css app.css --format json "p-4 px-2 py-2"
hello from a plugin
[
  {
    "input": "p-4 px-2 py-2",
    "output": "p-2",
    "changed": true
  }
]

$ printf 'p-4 px-2 py-2\nw-4 h-4\n' | npx tailwindcss canonicalize --css app.css --stream
hello from a plugin
p-2
size-4
```

I expect only the results on stdout, and the output of a plugin on stderr.

A real case: daisyUI prints a banner when it loads, unless its option `logs` is `false`. A formatter that reads one line per class list from `--stream` takes the banner as the first answer, and then writes each class list into the wrong element.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "`canonicalize`: `console.log` of a plugin lands in stdout, before the results" (#20560)

Issues.Title: Write plugin logs to stderr in `canonicalize`
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`tailwindcss canonicalize` writes its results to stdout, but the design system is loaded in the same process, so anything a plugin logs with `console.log` while it loads (e.g. the daisyUI banner) ends up in front of the results. That breaks `--format json` and shifts every line in `--stream` mode.

This points `console.log`, `console.info` and `console.debug` at `console.error` for the `canonicalize` command, so stdout only carries the results and plugin output goes to stderr.

Fixes #20560

## Test plan

Added an integration test with a plugin that calls `console.log`, it fails on `main` and passes with this change.

Also checked by hand with the reproduction from the issue:

```
$ tailwindcss canonicalize --css app.css "p-4 px-2 py-2" 2>/dev/null
p-2
$ printf 'p-4 px-2 py-2\nw-4 h-4\n' | tailwindcss canonicalize --css app.css --stream 2>/dev/null
p-2
size-4
```

Issues.Title: @property fallback detection matches current Safari Technology Preview: margin-trim: inline is no longer valid CSS
Issues.Body:
**What version of Tailwind CSS are you using?**

v4 (seen in v4.1.0 output, still on main)

**What build tool (or framework if it abstracts the build tool) are you using?**

N/A, the issue is in the emitted CSS

**What version of Node.js are you using?**

N/A

**What browser are you using?**

Safari Technology Preview 254 (WebKit trunk since 2026-08-21)

**What operating system are you using?**

macOS

**Reproduction URL**

[minimal-testcase](https://bug-327332-attachments.webkit.org/attachment.cgi?id=481771)

This is affecting chatgpt.com and probably plenty of other sites.

**Describe your issue**

The `@property` fallback block is wrapped in

```
@supports ((-webkit-hyphens: none) and (not (margin-trim: inline))) or ((-moz-orient: inline) and (not (color:rgb(from red r g b))))
```

https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/blob/main/packages/tailwindcss/src/ast.ts

The Safari branch assumes `margin-trim: inline` is valid in every Safari that supports `@property`. **That is no longer true**. 

The CSS WG removed the inline values from margin-trim (https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13731), the [grammar is now](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box-4/#margin-trim) `none | block | [ block-start || block-end ]`, and all three engines follow it:

- WebKit: https://commits.webkit.org/319622@main (Safari Technology Preview, future Safari releases)
- Chromium: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8256869, `margin-trim` shipped to stable afterwards
- Firefox: block values only, behind a pref

So `CSS.supports('margin-trim', 'inline')` is now `false` in Safari Technology Preview, and the fallback block applies in a browser that supports `@property`. Chrome and Firefox are not affected, since Chrome does not support `-webkit-hyphens` and Firefox supports `rgb(from ...)`.

When the properties layer comes first, the fallback is harmless. When it ends up after the utilities layer, the `* { --tw-*: ... }` resets win over the utilities. This happens on chatgpt.com today, where every `-translate-y-1/2` is lost in Safari Technology Preview and controls are drawn half their height too low.

Expected: the fallback does not apply in browsers that support `@property`.

A detection that does not depend on margin-trim's inline values would fix it. Already deployed CSS will keep the old condition, so we are also discussing a [compatibility workaround on the WebKit side](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=327332).
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "@property fallback detection matches current Safari Technology Preview: margin-trim: inline is no longer valid CSS" (#20568)

Issues.Title: Use `margin-trim: block` in the `@property` fallback detection
Issues.Body:
Fixes #20568.

## Summary

The `@property` fallback is gated on `not (margin-trim: inline)`. The CSSWG removed the inline values (w3c/csswg-drafts#13731), and Safari Technology Preview now rejects them, so the fallback resets override utilities there.

This switches to `margin-trim: block`. That value is still in the grammar and shipped with `@property` in [Safari 16.4](https://webkit.org/blog/13966/webkit-features-in-safari-16-4/), so the branch still matches only older Safari. Firefox's branch is unchanged.

I did not use `at-rule(@property)`: browsers without `at-rule()` support would evaluate `not at-rule(…)` as true.

## Test plan

- `pnpm vitest run packages/tailwindcss/src/index.test.ts -t 'fallback detection'`: fails on `main`, passes here.
- `pnpm vitest run packages/tailwindcss`: 5107 passed, 1 skipped; snapshots updated for the new string.
- Not run locally: the `@tailwindcss/postcss` tests and the integration tests (no oxide native build here).

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude), reviewed and tested before submission.

Issues.Title: Fix canonicalization of `theme(…)` alpha with more than 2 decimals
Issues.Body:
## Summary

This PR fixes two problems with how an inline `theme(…)` alpha is canonicalized to a candidate modifier.

### Alphas with more than 2 decimals

When canonicalizing an arbitrary property that uses an inline `theme(…)` with a fractional alpha that has more than 2 decimals, the opacity changed by a factor of 100.

For example, `[color:theme(colors.red.500/.12345)]` became `text-red-500/1234.5`. An arbitrary modifier without a unit is treated as a number and multiplied by 100, so the result had an opacity of `1234.5%` instead of `12.345%`.

This PR uses an arbitrary percentage instead, so `[color:theme(colors.red.500/.12345)]` now becomes `text-red-500/[12.345%]`.

While working on this, I also noticed floating point noise: `.29 * 100` is `28.999999999999996`, which would also have produced an arbitrary modifier. The value is now rounded first, so `[color:theme(colors.red.500/.29)]` becomes `text-red-500/29`.

### Custom `--opacity-*` theme values

A named modifier like `/50` reads from the `--opacity-*` theme values first. So if a theme already defines `--opacity-50: 10%`, then `[color:theme(colors.red.500/50%)]` became `text-red-500/50`, which is a 10% opacity instead of 50%. The same happened for `.12` → `/12` and `.29` → `/29`.

Now the named modifier is only used when there is no `--opacity-*` theme value for it, or when that value results in the same opacity (e.g. `--opacity-75: 0.75` or `--opacity-75: 75%`). Otherwise, an arbitrary percentage is used:

| Theme | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| no `--opacity-50` | `[color:theme(colors.red.500/50%)]` | `text-red-500/50` |
| `--opacity-50: 10%` | `[color:theme(colors.red.500/50%)]` | `text-red-500/[50%]` |
| `--opacity-75: 0.75` | `[color:theme(colors.red.500/75%)]` | `text-red-500/75` |

## Test plan

- Updated the existing `.12345` case and added a `.29` case in `canonicalize-candidates.test.ts`.
- Added cases with conflicting, matching and missing `--opacity-*` theme values, for both `@theme` and `@theme inline`. The conflicting cases fail on `main`.

```
pnpm vitest run packages/tailwindcss/src/canonicalize-candidates.test.ts
```
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Fix canonicalization of `theme(…)` alpha with more than 2 decimals" (#20563)

Issues.Title: Fix the intersection polyfill in canonicalizeCandidates
Issues.Body:
## Summary

The `intersection` helper in `canonicalize-candidates.ts` falls back to a polyfill when `Set.prototype.intersection` is missing (Node.js < 22). The polyfill copied the first set and never removed any item, so it returned the first set instead of the intersection. The collapse step gave different results on those Node.js versions.

The polyfill now keeps only the items of the first set that are also in the second set. The function is exported so the polyfill path can be tested directly.

## Test plan

Added unit tests for the polyfill path (the native method is stubbed out).

```
cd packages/tailwindcss
pnpm vitest run src/canonicalize-candidates.test.ts
```

Issues.Title: Fix the Nuxt dev mode integration test
Issues.Body:
## Summary

The `vite/nuxt.test.ts > dev mode` integration test fails on `main` on Linux, macOS and Windows since Vite 6.4.4 (released on 2026-10-06). The SSR render of `/` crashes, so the page has no styles:

```
[GET] "http://[::1]:3000/__nuxt_vite_node__/module//node_modules/.pnpm/ofetch@1.5.1/node_modules/ofetch/dist/node.mjs": 403 Forbidden
```

Nuxt 3.16.0 serves vite-node modules over HTTP. For each module id, it calls Vite's `isFileServingAllowed(config, id)`. These ids are root-relative URLs, like `/node_modules/.pnpm/...`. Before Vite 6.4.4, the import analysis plugin added these URLs to `safeModulePaths`, so the check passed. Vite 6.4.4 adds the resolved file paths instead (https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/23656), so the check now rejects the root-relative ids.

All Nuxt versions before 3.18.0 do this check. Nuxt 3.18.0 and later serve vite-node modules over an IPC socket without it. This PR moves the test to Nuxt 3.21.11, the latest 3.x release. It runs on Vite 7.3.7, which has the same `safeModulePaths` change.

It also removes the `nitropack: 2.11.0` pin. Nuxt 3.21 gets Nitro through `@nuxt/nitro-server` (`nitropack@^2.13.4`), so nothing used the pinned copy.

## Test plan

Locally on macOS, with `pnpm vitest --root=./integrations run vite/nuxt.test.ts`:

- Nuxt 3.16.0 and Vite 6.4.4: `dev mode` fails with the same 403 as CI.
- Nuxt 3.16.0 with a `vite: 6.4.3` override: both tests pass. This confirms the cause.
- Nuxt 3.21.11: both tests pass in 3 of 3 runs, with and without the `nitropack` pin.

CI checks Linux and Windows.

[ci-all]
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Fix the Nuxt dev mode integration test" (#20564)

Issues.Title: Underline the correct occurrence of an unsupported type in --value
Issues.Body: ## Summary When a `@utility` uses an unsupported bare value data type in `--value(…)`, Tailwind warns and prints the expression with a `^^^` underline under the bad type. If the same type appears more than once, every warning underlines the *first* occurrence: ```css @utility paint-* { paint: --value(color, [color], color); } ``` Before, both warnings pointed at the first color: ``` --value(color, [color], color) ^^^^^ ``` This happened because the underline position came from cloning the function node and replacing every word whose value matched the type with a placeholder. The code then used `indexOf` on that placeholder, which always finds the first match. Now the placeholder only goes into the node being reported. That node's value is swapped for the placeholder, the expression is printed to find the offset, and then the original value is put back. Each warning now points at its own occurrence: ``` --value(color, [color], color) ^^^^^ --value(color, [color], color) ^^^^^ ``` ## Test plan Added a test in `packages/tailwindcss/src/utilities.test.ts`. It spies on `console.warn` and checks that the two warnings underline the first and the last color respectively. ``` cd packages/tailwindcss pnpm vitest run src/utilities.test.ts -t "repeated unsupported data type" ``` ## Evidences https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-yq34h5eo?file=input.css
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Underline the correct occurrence of an unsupported type in --value" (#20553)
